selection_rule: Every statement by an in-scope officeholder quoted in a story published on Nov. 14 or 15, 2026 in the NPR Politics and PBS NewsHour Politics feeds, and every statement by an in-scope guest in the Nov. 15, 2026 transcripts of CBS Face the Nation, NBC Meet the Press, ABC This Week and CNN State of the Union, as read on Nov. 15. PBS NewsHour carries Associated Press reporting. Only what a guest said live on a show is included, not clips played by the host. A claim one speaker repeated in similar words is listed once, with the other wordings beneath it. Two NPR audio segments with no transcript were skipped. Quotes under five words were left out, and two entries that were a commentator's account of what an official said were removed. Statements from the feeds' stories are worded as the outlet reported them unless a transcript is linked. Factual statements not yet checked are marked so and are checked in turn.
lede: This page lists 198 statements by 20 officeholders. 56 appeared in two days of NPR and PBS NewsHour politics coverage; the other 142 are from the Nov. 15 transcripts of four Sunday shows: CBS Face the Nation, NBC Meet the Press, ABC This Week and CNN State of the Union. Most were about the Nov. 13 nationwide ground stop and what it will cost to fix air traffic control, the Iran war, sales of advanced computer chips to China, and what the Nov. 3 election results mean.

111 statements have been checked: 32 supported, 63 unsettled, 12 unsupported, 3 contradicted, 1 false. Unsettled means evidence was found but does not decide the claim. Unsupported means no evidence was found, which is not a finding that the statement is false. Contradicted means a primary source says otherwise on the specific point while some question remains open.

7 statements are linked to a direct counter-statement by another official on this page or to an official document that says otherwise. 2 statements are linked to a statement by the same speaker that cannot also be true. A link shows that two statements disagree on the same point. It is not a finding about which is right.

Where a speaker made the same claim more than once, it is listed once with the other wordings beneath it; 19 claims were condensed this way. The remaining 87 statements are opinions, predictions, promises and personal attacks. They are listed because they were said, not because they can be checked, and are folded under each speaker.

FROM officials.senate_race_results

evidence.label: officials.senate_race_results (U.S. Senate returns, 1976-2024)
evidence.sql:
SELECT state_postal,
       sum(case when leader_party_major='D' then 1 else 0 end) d_wins,
       max(case when leader_party_major='D' then year end) last_d,
       sum(case when leader_party_major='OTHER' then 1 else 0 end) oth,
       max(case when leader_party_major='OTHER' then year end) last_oth,
       sum(case when leader_party_major is null then 1 else 0 end) nullp
FROM officials.senate_race_results
WHERE is_decisive
GROUP BY state_postal
ORDER BY d_wins, state_postal

evidence.sql:
SELECT spender_name, candidate_name, candidate_state, support_oppose, SUM(amount) AS total, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM fec.independent_expenditures_current
WHERE amount_implausible IS NOT TRUE AND superseded_by_amendment IS NOT TRUE
  AND "year" = '2026' AND candidate_office='S' AND candidate_state IN ('MI','MN','IL')
  AND (UPPER(spender_name) LIKE '%UNITED DEMOCRACY%' OR UPPER(spender_name) LIKE '%FAIRSHAKE%' OR UPPER(spender_name) LIKE '%SENATE MAJORITY%' OR UPPER(spender_name) LIKE '%DSCC%' OR UPPER(spender_name) LIKE '%DEMOCRATIC SENATORIAL%')
GROUP BY spender_name, candidate_name, candidate_state, support_oppose
ORDER BY total DESC
